title: A staged course needs a placement step
statement: A course whose learners climb stages needs a way to decide where each starts, or every learner defaults to the lowest stage and a stage ceiling never does any work.
detail: A Grade 3 reading lesson design makes its writing stages available rather than assigned: each unit sets a ceiling, and a child works at whatever stage they can reach below it (`g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx`, lines 5-6). It notes that something has to decide where a child starts, that a short pre-reading placement is the obvious candidate but is not designed yet, and that without it every child defaults to the first stage and the ceiling never does any work (line 38). A Grade 9 lesson design specification lists how students reach their stage as a decision needed before build (`g9/sources/Year 9 ELA_ Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.md`, line 303).
against: Neither design has built the step: the Grade 3 placement is not designed yet, and the Grade 9 specification still lists assignment, a diagnostic or the student's own choice as options (`g9/sources/Year 9 ELA_ Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.md`, line 303).
